hints: Focus on the reaction type first, heating an alcohol with concentrated sulfuric acid causes elimination of water to form an alkene.
Draw out butan-2-ol as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and notice the OH can be lost with a H from C1 or from C3, giving two different positions for the double bond.

Remember that but-2-ene can exist as two different geometric forms depending on whether the two $\text{CH}_3$ groups are on the same side or opposite sides, so count positional plus stereoisomers together.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction as dehydration**

Heating with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from an alcohol to give an alkene. Think of it as removing OH from one carbon and H from a neighbouring carbon.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_8 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the positional isomers**

In butan-2-ol the OH is on C2. Remove H from C1 and you get but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$. Remove H from C3 and you get but-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$. These are structural isomers with the double bond in different places.

**Add stereoisomerism for but-2-ene**

But-2-ene has two different groups on each C of the double bond, $\text{CH}_3$ and H. This allows cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism. One form has both $\text{CH}_3$ groups on the same side (cis, Z) and the other has them on opposite sides (trans, E).

**Count the total structures**

We get one but-1-ene with no stereoisomers, plus two stereoisomers of but-2-ene. That is three alkene structures in total, and no branched chain product is possible without rearrangement.

options.A: Shows but-1-ene and only one form of but-2-ene (the trans form). This misses the cis form of but-2-ene, so it is incomplete. Students choosing this forget that but-2-ene shows geometric isomerism.
options.B: Shows all three correct products: cis-but-2-ene, trans-but-2-ene, and but-1-ene. This correctly combines positional isomerism (double bond at C1-C2 vs C2-C3) with cis-trans isomerism of but-2-ene.
options.C: Shows but-1-ene and only one form of but-2-ene (the cis form). This misses the trans form of but-2-ene, so it is incomplete. It is the mirror trap to option A.
options.D: Includes 2-methylpropene, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CH}_2$, which is branched. Dehydration of the straight chain butan-2-ol cannot give a branched skeleton without rearrangement of the carbon chain, so this structure is impossible here.
